_why: Locally installed tools the AI harnesses launch against, whose version is somebody else's fact changed on their own schedule with nothing here noticing. Sibling of model-catalog-sources.json: same L216 shape, one level down. That file keeps the harness's MODEL list current; this one keeps the harness's PROGRAMS current.
_how_to_add: Copy a row. `version_from.argv` is a command that prints a version, with `capture` a regex holding one group around it. `install.argv` is whatever this machine already uses to install that tool, so a different package manager is a different argv rather than a code change. `restart.argv` is optional and runs only when the version actually moved.
_no_machine_literals: argv[0] is a program NAME, never a path into somebody's home directory. A path typed here is one machine's fact frozen into shipped bytes: it is wrong for every other person, wrong for the same person after they move the tool, and the package compiler refuses it outright (BRTK3002_LOCAL_PATH_LEAK). Where the program lives is a question the machine answers, so name the program and, if it sits somewhere the PATH does not reach, say where with `program_search_paths`. Two machine facts may be named in any argument and the owner fills them in: `~` for the person's home directory, and `{current-user-id}` for their numeric user id.
_the_owner: do-work/converge-declared-local-tools-to-their-served-version.mjs, which names no tool, no installer and no service. Pass --tools-file to point it at a different declaration.

tools.why: Every ChatGPT-account request from Codex and the Desktop app goes through this proxy on port 2455, and it is what injects previous_response_id, so a stale copy is what kills a thread with 'Invalid previous_response_id' (upstream issue 395, closed fix-pending-release). Found on 1.22.0 on 2026-09-10, well behind the fix for the error it was producing.

version_from._note: The CLI itself has no version flag, so the installer is asked instead. That is why the readback is DATA: what can answer 'which version is installed' differs per tool and per installer.
